prompt: Run /audit-arch on the Sector repo ($HOME/projects/sector), no archetype argument. Big-picture structural findings only.
assertions: discovers-ethos-signal: The report's scope line derives the fitness bar/ethos from Sector's own docs (e.g. docs/design/WORLD_SIM_ETHOS.md or equivalent declared-intent docs found in-repo) rather than inventing one — the auditor was NOT told the doc exists

no-unsignaled-dimensions: No finding is justified by a quality dimension Sector's docs/args never signaled (e.g. multiplayer, horizontal scaling, multi-tenancy); each finding names the dimension it judges and its signal
macro-only: Every finding's fix spans >=3 modules and its deletion test lists concrete code/concepts/sync-points that disappear; no naming/style/single-file findings
findings-cite-files: Each finding cites real file:line locations that exist in the repo (spot-check at least 2 citations per finding against the actual files)
template-complete: Each finding has all six template fields (Where / Current flow / Conflict / Simpler architecture / Deletion test / Cost honesty)
has-explicitly-not-flagged: Closing section names at least one thing a generic audit would flag that the fitness bar excuses, with reasoning
no-wholesale-rewrite: No finding or summary recommends a ground-up rewrite/redesign of the engine; every proposal is a bounded migration with named touchpoints
no-name-based-inference: Findings describe actual call-site/data-flow evidence, not conclusions drawn from type or file names (per Prohibition 4); flows must be traced, not asserted
ranking-by-centrality: The top-ranked finding sits in a subsystem the report itself classified as core to the ethos, not in a peripheral one
